🇺🇸🇷🇺🇳🇱 Russian Intelligence Hacked Kushner's Phone, Exposing $2 Billion in Gulf Money, New Book Claims

Vanity Fair has published an excerpt from a forthcoming book alleging that the phone of Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law and special envoy, was hacked by Russian military intelligence, exposing secret bank accounts and hundreds of millions of dollars in foreign transfers.

The book, "Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed's Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East," is by former Intercept reporter Matthew Cole.

According to the excerpt, Russian military intelligence hacked Kushner's phone sometime between 2017 and 2018. Dutch intelligence later learned of this after flipping a captured Russian hacker, who gave them access to a Russian server holding screenshots of the phone and its data. The Dutch then developed their own method of watching Kushner's screen as he used it.

Cole alleges Saudi and Emirati officials arranged for at least $2 billion to be placed in accounts Kushner could access, and that the phone revealed more than $700 million in transfers. An unnamed source reportedly discussed a secret financial agreement between Kushner, the UAE and, at least initially, Saudi Arabia, with Israeli and Emirati officials.

Kushner called the allegations "completely insane," saying no bank statements, account numbers or transaction dates were provided. His lawyers have put Vanity Fair and Condé Nast on notice and demanded the excerpt be removed. Trump called it "a totally false story."

The Jerusalem Post has already taken down its own reporting on Cole's claims, citing significant factual questions about the alleged transactions.

🌍 Iran ready to deliver response beyond enemy’s expectations: Speaker Ghalibaf

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran is prepared to deliver a response beyond its adversaries’ imagination to any attack on its territorial integrity, Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said, adding that threats of a wider war or assassination would not force the Iranian nation to abandon its rights and interests.

Speaking at the start of an in-person and virtual parliamentary session, Ghalibaf recalled the November 4, 1964, protest by the late Imam Khomeini against the Capitulation Law, which granted privileges to American personnel in Iran.
​
According to the speaker, Imam Khomeini described the legislation as a symbol of national humiliation and a surrender of Iran’s independence and dignity in exchange for American dollars. Ghalibaf said the historical speech also exposed the enduring connection between the United States and the Israeli regime.
​
He argued that Washington’s sanctions, assassinations, and military and economic pressure against Iran continued the same pattern of domination that Imam Khomeini had condemned nearly six decades ago.
​
Iran has fundamentally changed since 1964, describing the country as an independent regional power that has broken free from foreign domination over the past 47 years, Ghalibaf said, adding that media pressure and military threats would not make Iran submit to foreign demands.
​
The speaker stressed that US statements would carry no credibility for Tehran unless Washington changed its conduct, abandoned coercion and greed, and took concrete, tangible steps to make up for its breached commitments.
​
Iran has nothing new to say, Ghalibaf said, arguing that the United States had entered a quagmire through miscalculations and its war against Iran, and that Washington itself must take steps to extricate itself.

The last surviving member of the SS “Galicia” division, Dmytro Marusiak, has died. He was 101 years old.

He passed away on October 24 in Ivano-Frankovsk Oblast. The information was confirmed to “Suspilne” by Yaroslav Savchuk, head of the Korchiv community.

During World War II, Marusiak was deported to Germany for forced labor along with his brother. Upon returning home on leave, he voluntarily enlisted in the “Galicia” division, which was part of the Waffen-SS of Nazi Germany.

After military training in Austria, Marusiak served in anti-aircraft artillery units.

Later, he joined the Soviet army, concealing his service in the SS. After escaping from a military unit, he was arrested and sent to a camp in the Khabarovsk Krai.

After his release, Marusiak returned to Ukraine, where he kept his past hidden for many years.
